RAD-only baseline · 15 October 2026                                                                        ii
1. Authority, identity and use

This publication answers: “What capability architecture does the governed RAD currently con-
tain?” Version 0.1 represents the current governed Markdown architecture without extending,
completing or reconciling it. The Markdown RAD remains architectural authority; this publica-
tion is its definitive LaTeX representation at the recorded baseline. The Architectural Axioms
remain the highest design authority.
AX-01 and AX-04 preserve the business and health-information meaning of the model. AX-
14 preserves distinctions between capability, behaviour, exposure, progression, relevance and
status. AX-17 requires established, candidate and unresolved assertions to remain distinguish-
able. AX-18 prevents integration/coordination from conferring domain authority. This publica-
tion applies those constraints to representation; it makes no architectural change. The selected
axiom text, metamodel and K9 decision are reproduced in the semantic-detail part.


1.1. Reading the model

Business Capabilities use only the explicitly established CT1 → CT2 → CT3 hierarchy. Regions
are contextual groupings, not ancestors. Business Enabling Capabilities require CT1 → CT2 →
CT3 → FT for a fully reconciled Feature, but the current RAD does not establish those BEC tier
allocations or complete ancestry. This publication preserves established owners and the ex-
plicit partial Client Administration → Person Identity responsibility chain without manufacturing
missing tiers. It reports zero established BEC CT1, CT2 or CT3 allocations; this does not mean
that the 76 established BEC contexts do not exist.
Functions, Services and Processes retain their evidenced owners. They form a graph, not a
mandatory Feature → Function → Service/Process tree. A Function need not have a Feature,
Service or Process association. Enterprise Capabilities retain the fourteen governed entries and
their actual descriptive responsibilities; no additional Enterprise decomposition is introduced.
Each element has a stable label, metadata and a link to exact RAD source detail. The semantic-
detail part preserves the source definitions, boundaries, state-change statements, illustrative
activities, examples, exclusions, notes, classifications, relationship tables and unresolved mat-
ters. Its source headings and retained diagram notation are not new containment assertions.
The complete manifest.json records exact source lines and fingerprints; source-coverage.json
records the transcribed blocks. Source references such as “business:152” mean source-key
and Markdown line, not a new architectural identifier.


1.2. Definitive publication identity

Existing Feature identifiers (for example FEAT-EM-01) and Enterprise identifiers (EC-01 through
EC-14) are preserved exactly. Catalogue ordinals, BC-18-style source shorthand and CT syntax
examples are not allocated structural Canonical IDs. No structural Canonical ID is allocated
here.
For elements without an allocated identifier, the frozen Reference Id uses HCM-type-semantic-
name-token. Type tokens are BC, BEC, FN, SV and PR. The initial token is the lowercase name
with runs of non-alphanumeric characters replaced by a hyphen. This is a deterministic initial
allocation rule only: after v0.1, the manifest value must be reused verbatim, including
after rename or relocation. It is not regenerated from a future name, parent, tier, ordinal,
chapter or build. A collision requires an explicitly recorded allocation, never a position-based
suffix; this baseline has no collisions.
The Reference Id is a definitive publication identity, distinct from the metamodel’s contextual
structural Canonical ID. The metamodel requires a structural ID to change when responsibility
Harmonia EA Capability Map                                                           Version 0.1


context changes, retaining the former value as an alias. Keeping these two fields separate
satisfies both that rule and publication identity stability. Unallocated or ancestry-dependent
structural IDs remain unresolved.
Stable LaTeX label namespaces are cap:bc-, cap:bec-, cap:ec-, feature:, function:, service: and
process:. The exact values are frozen in the manifest and are also preserved across relocation
or rename. Source-detail labels are locators, not architectural element identities. Internal
reference-candidate record keys are retained for navigation continuity only; they are neither
Canonical IDs nor aliases.


1.3. Architectural status and uncertainty

Canonical means that the element’s identity/responsibility is established by the cited governed
RAD. It does not establish every possible property or relationship of that element. Candidate
preserves a named provisional concern without approving its placement or decomposition. Un-
resolved qualifies a particular unestablished dimension or relationship. It is not a fifth Harmo-
nia relevance classification. Source-specific provisional proposals remain provisional in their
source prose; occurrence in a canonical document does not promote them to Canonical.
Health Service Governance is a Canonical CT1 with unresolved relevance and enabling deriva-
tion. The three assurance BECs are Canonical responsibilities with unresolved tiers, ancestry,
view placement, relevance and Feature decomposition. All 137 Features are established FT
identities with unresolved complete capability ancestry. The 69 enabling catalogue descrip-
tions with unestablished standalone element identity are not counted as new Capabilities.

Counts are of independently established identities or explicitly retained candidates, not source
occurrences, descriptive bullets or possible future peers. The reference candidate capture was
used to locate current Markdown evidence; its candidate standing supplies no architectural
approval. Counts and identifiers are checked against the actual Markdown inventories and
explicit parent assertions.


1.5. Preserved issues requiring later architectural review

The full source qualifications remain controlling. In particular:

• BEC tier/ancestry reconciliation, 137 Feature frames and 69 description identities remain
  unresolved under K9; the five views do not resolve them.
• Health Information Exchange identifies distinct BC and BEC responsibilities. Their naming
  collision remains unresolved; they are not merged or renamed.


RAD-only baseline · 15 October 2026                                                            2
Harmonia EA Capability Map                                                           Version 0.1


• Medication compounding/preparation (OI-BC-001), operational-readiness placement (OI-BC-
  002), maintenance membership and sharing-programme placement remain unadjudicated.
  Clinical Intervention’s proposed three-child taxonomy remains provisional; Clinical Determi-
  nation and Individual Care Planning have no adjudicated CT3 set.
• Operational Credential Management remains distinct from Clinical Qualification Management
  and its historical name alias. Name similarity does not establish Feature association.
• The existing care-team collaboration Function description mentions managing clinical han-
  dovers while the metamodel excludes that authority. Both source assertions are retained
  for review; this publication does not resolve the conflict.
• Process illustrations retain their stated scope and unresolved transitions, including Encounter
  ON_LEAVE and the disconnected stalled/failed Synthetic Task outcome. Assurance lifecycle
  detail and internal Service/Function mappings remain unestablished; no additional state or
  edge is inferred.
• The assurance Strategy source’s opening reconciliation qualifies older BC-18 tier/relevance
  wording. Its Strategy stop boundary does not erase the later approved Domain03 assur-
  ance catalogue. B2.1’s retained L1/L2 terminology does not allocate or override current CT
  classifications.

No legacy documentation or architectural material from the earlier candidate LaTeX publications
was used. Version 0.2 derivation and reconciliation are outside this baseline.

2. Business Capabilities

The hierarchy below contains only explicit governed BC tier and parent assertions. Full defi-
nitions, decomposition assertions, boundaries, illustrative activities, care contexts, exclusions
and stopping points are reproduced in the BC source detail. Relevance is not inherited. Regions
are contextual groupings.

tion, not a CT assertion. Features, Functions, Services and Processes below retain their actual
owning context. Function/Service/Process and Feature associations form a graph, recorded in
the relationship register. A Feature listing is not a claim of complete CT1 → CT2 → CT3 → FT
reconciliation.

4. Enterprise Capabilities

These are the fourteen governed reusable architectural capabilities. Functional responsibility
bullets are descriptive responsibilities, not additional named Function or Service identities. No
CT decomposition or additional Enterprise peers are inferred.

Capability Metadata
Name                   Value                                     Comment / Description
Reference Id           EC-01                                     Stable publication identity.
Architectural Status   Canonical                                 Established by RAD.
Source                 enterprise:103 (p. 465)                   Linked RAD detail; exact
                                                                 locators in manifest.

• Architectural Scope: Identify, classify, relate, and maintain the structural integrity of man-
  aged healthcare and administrative entities throughout the enterprise landscape.

• Architectural Scope: Identify, classify, relate, and maintain the structural integrity of man-
  aged healthcare and administrative entities throughout the enterprise landscape.
• Functional Responsibilities:
   • Uniquely identifying core domain entities (Persons, Practitioners, Roles, Organisations,
     Locations, Services, Devices).
   • Resolving and maintaining multi-authority identifier systems and aliases without destruc-
     tive overwriting.
   • Representing and traversing multi-dimensional relationships (affiliations, organizational
     hierarchies, physical location trees, care team memberships).
   • Maintaining referential integrity across interconnected entity graphs.
• Anti-Responsibilities: Does not own physical database relational tables or foreign key
  constraints (Domain 04/07).

Harmonia EA Capability Map                                                              Version 0.1


Capability Metadata
Name                   Value                                      Comment / Description
Reference Id           EC-07                                      Stable publication identity.

Source                 enterprise:157 (p. 467)                    Linked RAD detail; exact
                                                                  locators in manifest.

• Architectural Scope: Preserve required origin attribution, meaningful transformation his-
  tory, significant execution checkpoints, tamper-evident audit evidence and end-to-end trace-
  ability. Harmonia SHALL preserve provenance, audit and operational evidence where re-
  quired by governing obligations, architectural significance, accountability, reconstruction,

  durable evidentiary recording.

• Architectural Scope: Preserve required origin attribution, meaningful transformation his-
  tory, significant execution checkpoints, tamper-evident audit evidence and end-to-end trace-
  ability. Harmonia SHALL preserve provenance, audit and operational evidence where re-
  quired by governing obligations, architectural significance, accountability, reconstruction,
  security or assurance needs. Routine technical activity SHALL NOT automatically require
  durable evidentiary recording.
• Functional Responsibilities:
   • Recording attributable, verifiable origin metadata for information sources, authors, and
     timestamps.
   • Tracking information-significant transformation history and required mapping checkpoints
     as information crosses system seams.
   • Capturing non-PHI operational and security audit trails for regulatory compliance (HIPAA,
     GDPR).
   • Supporting end-to-end transaction tracing across asynchronous processing pipelines.
• Collaborative Nature: Participating elements preserve required provenance and audit con-
  text according to policy. Telemetry, operational facts, provenance, audit and assurance
  evidence remain distinct. Being evidence is contextual, not an intrinsic property of every
  recorded fact; preservation does not establish an assurance conclusion.

EC-12 / EC-14 Boundary

EC-12 retains the established scope and responsibilities above. It may contribute directly to
generic operational/processing assurance, limited to that contribution in the approved assur-
ance matrix. It does not own the general semantics of assurance disposition, assurance-specific
criteria applicability, evidentiary association, assessment against assurance criteria, adjudica-
tion, or independent assurance findings and conclusions. Those distinguishing responsibilities
are introduced through EC-14 Service Guardian. Operational health and business-level process-
ing assurance remain distinct; EC-12 is not expanded to absorb EC-14.

4.14. Service Guardian

Capability Metadata
Name                   Value                                     Comment / Description
Reference Id           EC-14                                     Stable publication identity.
Architectural Status   Canonical                                 Established by RAD.
Source                 enterprise:224 (p. 469)                   Linked RAD detail; exact
                                                                 locators in manifest.

• Architectural Scope: Service Guardian provides the reusable capability to independently
  establish whether governed service behaviour, state or outcomes remain within defined
  assurance expectations by associating applicable criteria and trustworthy evidence with a
  governed subject, assessing that evidence, adjudicating the assessment, and establishing
  reportable assurance findings and conclusions.

• Architectural Scope: Service Guardian provides the reusable capability to independently
  establish whether governed service behaviour, state or outcomes remain within defined
  assurance expectations by associating applicable criteria and trustworthy evidence with a
  governed subject, assessing that evidence, adjudicating the assessment, and establishing
  reportable assurance findings and conclusions.



RAD-only baseline · 15 October 2026                                                             275
Harmonia EA Capability Map                                                            Version 0.1


• Functional Responsibilities:
   • Supplying assurance-specific semantics for assurance disposition and assurance criteria
     applicability.
   • Associating a governed subject/context with applicable criteria and sufficient trustworthy
     evidence for a particular assurance purpose.
   • Assessing evidence against applicable criteria and adjudicating assessed detail to estab-
     lish reportable findings, exceptions and conclusions.
   • Preserving assurance independence, temporal/version-specific evidence and criteria ap-
     plicability, and explicit inability to establish a conclusion where evidence is insufficient.
• Collaborative Nature: Supplies the assurance-specific semantics required to bind existing
  reusable capabilities into governed assurance. It contributes directly to Assurance Design,
  Assurance Criteria Management and Governed Assurance; direct contribution is not sole
  realisation. The approved matrix preserves the contributions of EC-01 through EC-13.
• Anti-Responsibilities: Does not own the underlying governed subject, authoritative gov-
  ernance requirements, or source information used as evidence. Does not perform, manage,
  remediate, assign, delegate or operationally escalate the subject activity. Does not replace
  System Operations or EC-12 Operational Assurance, and does not provide Clinical Services
  Delivery Assurance.
• Allocation Boundary: No strategic logical component, application component, runtime
  service or implementation construct is allocated EC-14. The catalogue defines a capability,
  not a software component or deployment boundary.


Conceptual Behavioural Sequence

RAD source listing (presentation only; no inferred ancestry).
     Define Good Behaviour
     ↓
     Gather Evidence
     ↓
     Assess Evidence against Good Behaviour
     ↓
     Adjudicate Assessed Detail
     ↓
     Report
This sequence explains the capability; it is not an implementation workflow specification or
a derived Business Process. “Define Good Behaviour” identifies assurance expectations and
criteria; it does not transfer ownership of governing requirements to Service Guardian. Source
information ownership remains with its responsible capability; assurance owns its contextual
evidentiary association.
The Business Enabling assurance principles govern disposition, generic processing assurance,
evidence/criteria temporality, assessment/adjudication, independence, failure/recovery and
explicit evidence insufficiency. These semantics are not universally reducible to PASS / FAIL
/ UNKNOWN and do not imply an assurance information model or persistence mechanism.

tionship types.

8. Canonical Business Capability Model (18 CT1 Domains)

RAD source: docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-capabilities.md
The following is a presentation transcription of the governed source. Source catalogue layout
and retained illustrations do not allocate tiers or establish additional identities. Equations wrap
as text; diagram notation is textual.


Canonical Business Capability Model (18 CT1 Domains)

Overview & Purpose

Business Capabilities describe what the health enterprise/business must be capable of
doing. They are organisational abilities independent of technology, products, departments,
professions or automation. This catalogue is the canonical R1/R2 reconciliation of the adjudi-
cated Business Capability decisions recorded in DN-BC-001 through DN-BC-037. The scratchpad
retains working reasoning only; the definitions, explicit tier/parent assertions and boundaries
here govern the reconciled model. Provisional and unresolved matters are not promoted as
approved hierarchy.
Business Enabling Capabilities describe reusable enabling abilities Harmonia provides or
supports. The two hierarchies are distinct:
RAD source listing (presentation only; no inferred ancestry).
     Business Capability: CT1 → CT2 → CT3
     enabled-by / supported-by
     Business Enabling Capability: CT1 → CT2 → CT3 → Feature
The relationship is enablement/support, never decomposition or implementation equivalence.
Business Capabilities do not decompose into Harmonia Features. Features are ulti-
mately framed by Business Enabling CT3s. This catalogue establishes no new BC↔BEC map-
ping and does not reframe existing Features. Previously approved B2.1 and assurance support
relationships retain their bounded authority without being extended to the new BC descendants.
Technology-sounding names such as Health Information Exchange, Digital Communication
Channel, Identity Assurance and Access Control Enforcement describe organisational abili-
ties. Physical, procedural and digital mechanisms illustrate exercise/enablement, not software-
component identities. An interpretation requiring a particular software product to explain a BC
is suspect. Where BC and BEC concern the same subject, their names must distinguish organ-
isational ability from system enablement where reuse would imply equivalence or ownership.
The existing Exchange name collision is explicitly unresolved below.


R1/R2 Scope and Decomposition Rules

     Capability decomposition SHALL be sufficient to establish Harmonia’s architectural
     context and derivation requirements. It SHALL NOT pursue exhaustive decomposition
     of healthcare-enterprise capabilities where additional detail does not materially affect
     Harmonia responsibility, information semantics, interoperability, security, workflow
     enablement, traceability or another Harmonia architectural concern.

     Scope may determine decomposition depth. Scope must not distort decomposition
     semantics.
Harmonia EA Capability Map                                                             Version 0.1


The stopping test asks whether distinguishing another ability would materially change how Har-
monia behaves, governs, represents, exchanges, secures, coordinates or traces something.
Once a branch is decomposed, its materially distinct peers must be coherent from the busi-
ness perspective, independently of Harmonia’s implementation interest. This does not require
identical depth, a Feature for every peer or a complete healthcare-enterprise taxonomy. An
undecomposed CT1/CT2 does not authorise a skipped tier or an invented CT3.
The metamodel governs tier meaning. Explicit CT1/CT2/CT3 and parent statements below es-
tablish the stated BC hierarchy; display ordinals, indentation and regional membership alone
do not. CT4 and deeper tiers are outside scope. No ordinal is an allocated local code or Canon-
ical ID. BEC tiers/ancestry remain separately unresolved under K9. Absent decomposition does
not deny real-world abilities or assign them to an existing node.


Capability Modelling Quality Rules

Rule                               Requirement
CM-R01 Coverage                    Preserve the eighteen broad enterprise domains and five regions;
                                   decomposition is bounded by R1/R2 semantic sufficiency rather
                                   than exhaustive enterprise detail.
CM-R02 Orthogonality               Preserve distinct responsibilities, outcomes and authority even
                                   where capabilities share evidence, context or implementation
                                   machinery.
CM-R03 Semantic Clarity            Use clear business meanings; examples do not redefine
                                   capabilities as technology.
CM-R04 No Junk Drawers             Keep cohesive purposes; do not use residual categories to hide
                                   materially distinct abilities.
CM-R05 Global Name Uniqueness      Capability names are globally unique across the architecture.
                                   The unresolved BC/BEC Exchange collision is reported; neither
                                   identity is merged or renamed here.



Capability decomposition and educational documentation

Decomposition follows architectural distinction, not explanatory detail. Definition, state
change, boundary, illustrative activities, care contexts and exclusions explain capabilities with-
out establishing more children. History-taking, diagnosis, prescribing, medication administra-
tion, surgery, therapy and counselling are examples unless an explicit adjudication establishes
a Capability identity.


B2-R05 — Capability Is Independent of Care Delivery Context

Setting, delivery mode, temporal pattern and organisational arrangement do not by themselves
establish separate Business Capabilities.


B2-R06 — Context Independence Test

If changing setting, mode or time context does not materially change the business ability, it
remains the same Capability. Acute, Planned/Scheduled and Longitudinal Care are not Indi-
vidual Care Delivery’s CT2 decomposition. Inpatient, ambulatory, community, home, virtual,
emergency and elective remain illustrative contexts.

An established classification has exactly one of these values. Unresolved is a status, not a
fifth value. CT1 relevance describes material participation across its bounded scope; it does
not classify every descendant identically or confer enterprise-domain authority. Descendant
relevance remains unallocated unless explicitly established. Contextual resource/state con-
sumption alone warrants neither Core nor automatic Relevant classification. AX-18 preserves
originating and domain authority. A Harmonia-Core enabling responsibility may support a
Harmonia-Relevant BC without Harmonia owning that business activity.

ancestors, organisational boundaries or application ownership. They are distinct from the five
BEC contextual views. All eighteen named catalogue domains below are explicitly CT1 roots;
each branch statement explicitly establishes its CT2 parent and each table its CT3 parent.

Region 1: Care & Health Delivery

01. Individual Care Delivery

Tier and ancestry: CT1 root.
Definition: Assess, clinically determine, plan, intervene, monitor and review individual care
independently of setting, mode, time pattern or organisational arrangement.
Classification: Harmonia-Relevant.
The six CT2s are Individual Health Assessment, Clinical Determination, Individual Care Planning,
Clinical Intervention, Individual Health Monitoring and Individual Care Review. Their semantic
state changes do not prescribe execution order.


01.01 Individual Health Assessment

Tier and ancestry: CT2; parent Individual Care Delivery (CT1).
Definition: The capability to establish an understanding of an individual’s current health state
through the collection, consideration and evaluation of relevant clinical, health and contextual
information.
State Change: Healthinformation→Assessedhealthstate/findings
Boundary: Assessment establishes the assessed health state or findings. Existing records can
contribute, while direct examination, observation, history-taking or measurement may estab-
lish information independently of Health Information Access.
Illustrative Activities: History taking, physical examination, consideration of available clini-
cal records and measurement of current observations.
Example Care Contexts: An emergency presentation, a scheduled consultation or a home
visit may exercise the same assessment ability.
Explicit Exclusions: Establishing clinical conclusions, selecting the care response and per-
forming an intervention are not the assessment itself.


01.02 Clinical Determination

Tier and ancestry: CT2; parent Individual Care Delivery (CT1).
Definition: The capability to interpret assessed health information and establish clinically
meaningful conclusions about an individual’s health state, condition, risk or prognosis.
State Change: Assessedfindings→Clinicallyinterpretedunderstanding
Boundary: Clinical Determination interprets findings and establishes their clinical meaning,
including the clinical significance of change identified by monitoring.
Illustrative Activities: Diagnosis, clinical risk interpretation and prognostic judgement.


RAD-only baseline · 15 October 2026                                                          323
Harmonia EA Capability Map                                                           Version 0.1


Example Care Contexts: Interpretation during acute care or a longitudinal follow-up consul-
tation remains the same business ability.
Explicit Exclusions: Clinical Determination does not include establishing care needs or se-
lecting the response to the determination.


01.03 Individual Care Planning

Tier and ancestry: CT2; parent Individual Care Delivery (CT1).
Definition: The capability to establish the intended clinical response to an individual’s as-
sessed and clinically interpreted health state, including the objectives, interventions and mon-
itoring required to progress their care.
State Change: Clinicallyinterpretedunderstanding→Intendedcourseofcare
Boundary: Planning establishes what is intended to happen. It does not imply that the planned
care has occurred.
Illustrative Activities: Establishing care objectives, selecting intended therapy, prescribing
as an expression of clinical intent and planning monitoring.
Example Care Contexts: An intended course of care may be established during an inpatient
encounter, an ambulatory consultation or a virtual consultation.
Explicit Exclusions: Performing planned care is Clinical Intervention. Ordering, requesting,
scheduling and allocating care do not themselves establish that an intervention has occurred.
Operational service/resource availability information is not Health Information Access merely
because it informs planning.


01.04 Clinical Intervention

Tier and ancestry: CT2; parent Individual Care Delivery (CT1).
Definition: The capability to perform clinical actions intended to alter, maintain or otherwise
manage an individual’s health state in accordance with an established care intent.
State Change: Intendedcare→Careactionperformed
Boundary: Clinical Intervention establishes that a care action was performed. An intervention
need not produce a successful clinical outcome. Access to an intended intervention does not
confer authority to perform it.
Illustrative Activities: Medication administration, surgery, therapy and counselling when
performed as clinical actions under an established care intent.
Example Care Contexts: An intervention may be performed in inpatient, community or home
care, or through a suitable virtual delivery mode.
Explicit Exclusions: Ordering, requesting, scheduling or allocating an intervention is not itself
the Clinical Intervention; selecting the intended response belongs to planning.


01.05 Individual Health Monitoring

Tier and ancestry: CT2; parent Individual Care Delivery (CT1).
Definition: The capability to observe and evaluate an individual’s health state over time in
order to identify clinically meaningful change, stability or deviation from an expected state or
trajectory.
State Change: Observedhealthstatesovertime→Change/stability/deviationidentified
Boundary: Monitoring establishes change, stability or deviation. Interpretation of the clinical
significance of that change remains Clinical Determination.




RAD-only baseline · 15 October 2026                                                          324
Harmonia EA Capability Map                                                              Version 0.1


Illustrative Activities: Comparing serial observations with a baseline or expected trajectory
and identifying a trend or deviation.
Example Care Contexts: Serial inpatient observations and longitudinal home monitoring ex-
ercise the same ability across different time patterns and settings.
Explicit Exclusions: Clinical interpretation of an identified change and selection of the care
response are not monitoring. Evaluating care effectiveness against its objectives belongs to
Individual Care Review.


01.06 Individual Care Review

Tier and ancestry: CT2; parent Individual Care Delivery (CT1).
Definition: The capability to evaluate the progress and effectiveness of an individual’s care
against its intended objectives and establish the continuing appropriateness of the current care
intent.
State Change: Careprogress/outcomes→Effectivenessandcontinuingappropriatenessestablished
Boundary: Care Review evaluates the care itself against its intent and objectives; it is not
simply another name for reassessment.
Illustrative Activities: Reviewing response to delivered therapy against care objectives and
evaluating whether the current care intent remains appropriate.
Example Care Contexts: Review during an admission, a scheduled follow-up or longitudinal
care retains the same evaluation purpose.
Explicit Exclusions: Reassessment alone does not establish care effectiveness. Establishing
a revised intended course of care belongs to Individual Care Planning.
Clinical Determination and Individual Care Planning have no adjudicated CT3 set in the supplied
decisions. Clinical Intervention’s Therapy & Counselling Intervention / Medication Intervention
/ Procedural Intervention candidate remains provisional under DN-BC-010; it is not promoted
as a final taxonomy. Examples cannot close these gaps.
The previously approved B2.1 support trace is preserved without extending it to CT3s or estab-
lishing runtime dependencies.


CT2 — Individual Health Assessment

Tier and ancestry: CT2; parent Individual Care Delivery (CT1).
Definition: Establish an understanding of an individual’s current health state.
Decomposition assertion: Each named child in this table is a CT3 Business Capability whose
immediate CT2 parent is Individual Health Assessment; that CT2 has the CT1 parent stated
above.
CT3 Business Capability           Definition
Health History Assessment         Establish relevant health knowledge from the individual’s history
                                  and applicable historical/contextual information.
Clinical Examination              Establish health findings through clinical examination.
Health Status Measurement         Establish individual health observations or measurements.

Boundary: The decomposition distinguishes means of establishing knowledge. Functional, nu-
tritional, cognitive, mental-health and similar labels are assessment domains, not automatically
peer abilities. Risk interpretation belongs to Clinical Determination. Care setting, profession,
specialty and information type do not define the decomposition.


CT2 — Individual Health Monitoring

Tier and ancestry: CT2; parent Individual Care Delivery (CT1).



RAD-only baseline · 15 October 2026                                                             325
Harmonia EA Capability Map                                                              Version 0.1


Definition: Observe health over time to identify change, stability or deviation.
Decomposition assertion: Each named child in this table is a CT3 Business Capability whose

CT3 Business Capability            Definition
Health State Monitoring            Establish an aggregate, temporally situated view of the
                                   individual’s health from applicable monitored data.
Care Response Monitoring           Scope that health-state view to a particular problem/condition
                                   and the treatment applied to it.


Boundary: Care Response Monitoring consumes health-state services provided through Health
State Monitoring without independently recreating the aggregate view. This semantic con-
sumption establishes no named Service, interface or runtime invocation. Measurement sup-
plies observations; monitoring establishes a view; Clinical Determination interprets its clinical
significance. Deterioration, improvement and stability are possible monitored states, not es-
tablished peer CT3s.


CT2 — Individual Care Review

Tier and ancestry: CT2; parent Individual Care Delivery (CT1).
Definition: Evaluate care against intent and objectives.
Decomposition assertion: Each named child in this table is a CT3 Business Capability whose
immediate CT2 parent is Individual Care Review; that CT2 has the CT1 parent stated above.
CT3 Business Capability            Definition
Care Appropriateness Review        Evaluate whether the current intended care remains suitable in
                                   the individual’s current context.
Care Effectiveness Review          Evaluate whether delivered care is achieving or has achieved its
                                   intended goals and outcomes.


Boundary: An effectiveness finding may inform appropriateness without replacing it. Care
may be appropriate yet ineffective, or effective yet no longer appropriate to continue. Moni-
toring the response is distinct from judging effectiveness; identifying a need to reconsider care
does not establish the replacement plan. Replanning belongs to Individual Care Planning.


02. Care Access & Coordination

Tier and ancestry: CT1 root.
Definition: Managing patient intake, referral triage, appointment scheduling, multidisciplinary
care team coordination, cross-facility patient transfers, and care continuity across organisa-
tional boundaries.
Classification: Harmonia-Relevant.

of responsibility. Information assembly for clinical handover does not confer clinical-handover

03. Health Rights, Advocacy & Participation

Tier and ancestry: CT1 root.
Definition: Protecting patient rights, facilitating informed consent, managing advance care
directives, supporting patient advocacy, and enabling consumer participation in health deci-
sions.
Classification: Adjacent.
No CT2/CT3 set is established by this reconciliation. Consent and record-access evidence can
support rights without assigning advocacy or participation management to Harmonia.


04. Diagnostic, Therapeutic & Clinical Support Services

Tier and ancestry: CT1 root.
Definition: The specialised clinical services that support direct patient care, including pathol-

ing, and allied health therapies.
Classification: Harmonia-Relevant.
The following diagnostic and pharmacy branches are established. Other therapeutic/support
scope remains enterprise context; no further subordinate identity is manufactured.

fering may operate 06:00–22:00 while another pathway covers other hours. Offering availability
does not establish collective operational readiness; OI-BC-002 remains unplaced. Organisation,
location and practitioner associations do not substitute for material Healthcare Service context.

18. Health Service Assurance

Assurance Independence Reconciliation

Independence is a required property of applicable assurance approaches/evaluations, rather
than the exhaustive definition of the macro-level Business Capability. This does not make
Harmonia’s already-required independent governed assurance optional. REQ-FND-005 requires
it for activities, information and outcomes for which assurance is required. Its applicability
is bounded; it neither defines every enterprise assurance approach nor requires assurance of
every activity.
The approved Strategy derivation and Business assurance responsibilities implement that obli-
gation through independently governed progression and conclusion authority. Assurance Ap-
proach Definition may determine applicable methods, responsibilities and degree of indepen-
dence but SHALL NOT weaken those requirements. The subject may contribute evidence; it
shall not solely determine, suppress, manufacture or retrospectively alter its assurance out-
come. Evidence dependency is distinct from control dependency. No external assessor or
physical separation is implied.



RAD-only baseline · 15 October 2026                                                             344
Harmonia EA Capability Map                                                            Version 0.1


The broader organisational capability concerns justified confidence in service delivery. Harmo-
nia’s assigned participation remains assurance of explicitly required facts/behaviour; it does not
acquire clinical-adequacy assurance or management of the service. Thus the old independent-
evaluation definition is preserved as the established governed-assurance obligation within the
broader capability, rather than discarded or universalised to all enterprise evaluations. Op-
erational uncertainty under AX-15/REQ-FND-004 remains distinct from evidence insufficiency
under REQ-FND-005.


Clinical Services Delivery Assurance Boundary

Health Service Assurance SHALL NOT be represented as Clinical Services Delivery Assurance.
The enterprise scope’s reference to independent clinical audit/evaluation does not make Har-
monia responsible for assuring clinical judgement, professional practice, clinical adequacy of
care, or delivery of clinical services by healthcare practitioners or healthcare organisations.
Information concerning clinical service delivery MAY be the subject of governed assurance
where an explicit applicable requirement establishes that assurance concern. This does not
transfer responsibility for Clinical Services Delivery Assurance to Harmonia. Capability 06 —
Clinical Quality, Safety & Improvement retains its established clinical quality/safety responsi-
bilities.
     Harmonia may assure facts and behaviour concerning clinical activity where
     explicitly required; it does not thereby assure the clinical adequacy of care.


Meaning of Independent

Independent Assurance requires an independently governed assurance activity/workflow
whose progression and assurance conclusion are not controlled by the activity or mechanism
responsible for performing or managing the subject being assured.
Independence does not inherently require an external auditor, a different organisation, de-
partment, human actor, application, deployment, database or Kubernetes cluster, or physi-
cal infrastructure separation. This is a responsibility and authority boundary consistent with
REQ-FND-005, not an Application or Technology Architecture decision about physical execution
separation.
     Evidence dependency does not compromise assurance independence; con-
     trol dependency does.
The subject being assured may supply evidence. It shall not thereby be solely responsible for
determining, suppressing, manufacturing or retrospectively altering its assurance conclusion.


Assurance / Operational Management Boundary

Health Service Assurance does not thereby assume operational management of its subject, as-
signment, delegation, reassignment, operational escalation, operational remediation, workflow
progression, Incident Management or Incident Response. Findings, exceptions and conclusions
may inform or initiate appropriate operational activity; responsibility for that activity remains
with its operational capability.
     Assurance is the QA service, not the Job Foreman.
An assurance activity may manage its own internal assurance workflow without thereby as-
suming management of the subject being assured.

Unresolved Business Capability Matters

OI-BC-001 — Medication Compounding and Preparation

Unresolved. Whether compounding/specialised preparation warrants a distinct CT3 beneath
Medication & Pharmacy Services is neither established nor rejected. Absence does not mean
subsumption by Prescription Medication Dispensing, irrelevance, exclusion or representation by
another Capability. Adjudication must preserve peer completeness and the R1/R2 materiality
test.


OI-BC-002 — Health Service Operational Readiness Placement

The identified semantic concern asks: Can this Health Service Offering actually be de-
livered from this operational context? It establishes collective readiness from workforce,
administration, spaces, equipment/devices, materials, utilities, ICT/communications and other
dependencies without owning them. Ongoing site/service readiness and readiness for a session
are presently exercises of the same concern; session-level exercise does not establish another
Capability.
Its provisional name/identified identity and boundary are retained, but CT2 parent, CT1 an-
cestry and canonical placement remain unresolved. No complete CT1→CT2→CT3 path is
asserted. Offering defined/temporally available ≠ collectively ready; individual resource ready
≠ service ready; care-place readiness ≠ service readiness; readiness oversight ≠ clinical ex-
ecution or supporting-resource ownership. It SHALL NOT be placed beneath Health Service
Alignment, Healthcare Service Offering Management, Care Scheduling & Capacity Manage-
ment, Corporate Support Services, Health Product Management or another convenient parent
without explicit adjudication.

Semantic Relationships and Downstream Boundary

Business capabilities may provide evidence, context, identified events or established informa-
tion to other business capabilities while retaining their own outcomes and source authority.
Unless explicitly required otherwise, such provision is contextual rather than a universal de-
pendency. Information consumed ≠ ownership transferred; context supplied ≠ target
outcome established. These relationships are not decomposition, workflow order, runtime
invocation, Service identity or application dependency. Any RADS relationship must preserve
the exact meaning; where no governed type fits, preserve it as unresolved rather than substi-
tute a stronger convenient type.

Canonical Business Enabling Capability Model & Features

Overview & Architecture

The Business Enabling Capability model defines what systems and information infrastruc-
ture must enable or provide in support of the healthcare enterprise.
Where Business Capabilities define the high-level healthcare landscape (what the enterprise
does), Business Enabling Capabilities specify the functional abilities systems must deliver to
make healthcare delivery, administration, and operations possible.


Architectural Principles Governing this Model

1. Authentic Healthcare Operating Contexts: Capabilities are grouped into five authentic
   healthcare contextual views. They reflect genuine healthcare operating environments (e.g.,
   Ward Operations, Order Administration, Patient Clinical Record), not low-level integration
   engine plumbing or middleware mechanics.
2. Independence from Commercial Product Boundaries: Capabilities are defined inde-
   pendently of commercial software product boundaries (such as PAS, EMR, LIS, RIS, HRMS,
   or FMIS). A commercial product may implement multiple capabilities, drawing ”dotted lines”
   around parts of the model; the capability model remains orthogonal to vendor packaging.
3. Atomic Feature Decomposition: Within established Harmonia-Relevant and Harmonia-
   Core Capability contexts, system behaviour is decomposed into atomic Features—the
   smallest useful, testable, technology-neutral statements of system-enabled behaviour. Ref-
   erence and Adjacent capabilities are intentionally not decomposed into features.
4. Technology Neutrality: No capability or feature is defined in terms of specific software
   products (HAPI FHIR, Infinispan, PostgreSQL, ActiveMQ Artemis, Camel, Netty, Vue, Spring)
   or runtime plumbing (threads, queues, ports, DDL).
5. Architectural Scope Sufficiency: The Business Enabling Feature catalogue provides the
   established R1.x/R2.x Feature baseline for the capabilities and contextual views presently
   decomposed. Completeness SHALL NOT be interpreted as requiring artificial Feature decom-
   position of capabilities for which no Feature-level decomposition has been architecturally
   established. Roadmap items (such as authoritative master-patient EMPI reconciliation) are
   explicitly demarcated as uncommitted Harmonia 3.x candidates.

Under approved G1 K9, the five views, catalogue numbering, indentation and decomposition
presentation do not establish Architectural Element identity, CT1 / CT2 / CT3 assignment, an-
cestry or root status. The 137 established Features retain their FT type, names and identifiers.
Affected complete Capability ancestry and structural Canonical IDs remain unresolved. Deriva-
tion may proceed from established ownership and responsibility without inventing intermediate
elements.

The Five Contextual Views

The Business Enabling capabilities are structured across five contextual views:
RAD source listing (presentation only; no inferred ancestry).
     1. ENTITY MANAGEMENT
     Governance and administration of healthcare entities throughout
     their lifecycle: Clients, Providers, Organisations, Locations,
     Services, Products, and Devices.
     2. SERVICE ADMINISTRATION
     Administrative, logistical, and financial progression of care:
     Client Intake, Referrals, Encounters, Orders, Diagnostics,
     Care Plans, Clinical Messaging, and Billing Extraction.
     3. SERVICE DELIVERY
     Systems enablement across clinical delivery settings: Primary Care,
     Acute Inpatient, Emergency, Surgical, Diagnostic, Medication,
     Allied Health, Community, and Remote/Virtual Care.
     4. HEALTH SERVICE OPERATIONS
     Facility logistics, bed and care-place management, capacity,
     clinical resource coordination, work allocation and dispatch,
     patient transport, and discharge progression.
     5. INTRINSIC / SHARED ENABLEMENT
     Reusable system capabilities: Longitudinal Clinical Record,
     Health Information Exchange, Information Access, Policy & Security
     Control, Collaboration, Workflow Coordination, and Presentation.

1. Client Administration

Governs the representation, identification, and demographic context of individuals receiving

• 1.1 Person Identity (Harmonia-Core)
   • Definition: Resolving, maintaining, and correlating identities and identifiers assigned to

   • FEAT-EM-01: Identifier Resolution: Ingest and resolve external identifiers against regis-
     tered issuing authorities and namespace systems.
   • FEAT-EM-02: Cross-Authority Identifier Correlation: Correlate disparate local identi-
     fiers (e.g., hospital MRN, clinic client ID, national IHI) belonging to the same individual.
   • FEAT-EM-03: Identity Alias Association: Maintain explicit associations between active
     identifiers and historical or demographic aliases without destructive overwriting.
   • FEAT-EM-04: Governed Identity Correction: Apply administrative identity updates,
     linked-record corrections, and split/merge notifications propagated from authoritative
     sources.
• 1.2 Healthcare Subject (Harmonia-Core)
   • Definition: Managing the core healthcare subject context bound to clinical records and

     encounters, orders, and observations as the enduring subject of care with verifiable as-
     sociation.

     tributes (date of birth, sex, vital status) with full provenance and timestamping.

   • Definition: Representing relationships between the client and carers, guardians, or con-
     tacts.
   • FEAT-EM-07: Next-of-Kin & Guardian Association: Associate nominated emergency
     contacts, legal guardians, and care agents with the client record.

Critical Domain Distinctions: Service Administration

Distinction: Referral vs. Order

• Referral Administration: A Referral formally requests another care participant or service
  provider to assess, manage or assume some degree of clinical care responsibility. Referral
  intent, disposition, responsibility actually assumed and Transfer of Care are distinct. Referral
  may lead to shared or assumed responsibility or transfer of ongoing care, but does not itself
  establish acceptance, delivery, assumption or Transfer of Care, or universally require an
  Appointment, Encounter or Order.
• Order Administration: An Order requests a defined, bounded fulfilment activity (e.g.,
  execute a diagnostic test, dispense a medication, perform a procedure) and strictly supports
  a closed-loop progression returning an outcome to the requester.


Distinction: Technical ACK vs. Business ACK

• Technical Delivery Acknowledgement: A technical acknowledgement establishes only
  the acceptance state defined by the applicable interaction contract. It SHALL NOT be in-
  terpreted as durable acceptance, committed business state, successful processing or suc-
  cessful business disposition unless that meaning is explicitly established by the governing



RAD-only baseline · 15 October 2026                                                           359
Harmonia EA Capability Map                                                           Version 0.1


  contract. HTTP 200 does not universally establish successful business disposition, and HTTP
  202 does not universally establish durable queue acceptance; either may have stronger
  meaning under an explicit contract.
• Business Acknowledgement: A clinical/operational message generated by the receiving
  application or clinical staff confirming that the order or referral has been reviewed, accepted
  for execution, scheduled, or rejected. Technical Delivery Acknowledgement ≠ Business Ac-
  knowledgement

Acknowledgement of a handoff is not, by itself, evidence of eventual downstream business out-
come. REQ-FND-001 continues to require the applicable durable acceptance boundary before
Harmonia positively acknowledges ingress acceptance.
Business acknowledgement is contextual and may communicate acceptance, rejection or an-
other explicit disposition; it does not establish a universal reviewed → accepted → scheduled
progression or transfer originating authority.


Order Closed-Loop Progression Semantics

All order-related capabilities must support the end-to-end closed loop: Destination → Route →
Deliver → Acknowledge → Progress → Complete → Outcome

Architectural Principles: Service Delivery

1. Heterogeneous Axes Preserved: The 16 Service Delivery capabilities represent hetero-
   geneous clinical settings (acute, emergency, primary), modalities (virtual, outreach), and
   specialties (diagnostic, therapeutic). They are deliberately preserved as authentic health-
   care contexts rather than normalized into artificial abstractions.
2. Zero Harmonia-Core in Service Delivery: No Service Delivery capability is classified as Ha
   rmonia-Core. Harmonia provides integration, transport, state management, and notification;
   Harmonia does not practice medicine or deliver clinical therapy.
3. Canonical Enabling Pattern for Relevant Features: Provide Context → Receive Clinical
   State/Outcome → Correlate → Preserve Provenance → Make Available → Enable Next Activity

Architectural Principles: Health Service Operations

1. Facility Logistics, Not IT Machinery: Health Service Operations reflects real-world health
   facility logistics and coordination (wards, beds, staff allocation, patient transfer); it must
   never be redefined or reinterpreted as protocol mediation, message queuing, deduplication,
   or integration software machinery.
2. Healthcare Service Context Rule:

     Where operational activity occurs in the context of a Healthcare Service,
     that service context must be explicitly associated with the activity and state
     rather than inferred solely from practitioner, organisation, or location.

1. General Operational Progression Pattern: Event → Entity Context → Required Activity →
   Assignment → Dispatch → ACK → Progress → Outcome → Entity State Change → Next Activity

Critical Domain Distinctions: Intrinsic / Shared Enablement

Health Information Exchange: Four Interaction Models

1. Submission: ”I send this to you.” (Point-to-point push of an authored artifact).
2. Retrieval: ”I ask for this.” (Synchronous or asynchronous pull of specific records).
3. Distribution: ”I deliberately send this to identified recipients.” (Addressed fan-out delivery
   to designated systems or clinical actors).
4. Syndication: ”I publish information/change and subscribers receive matching interests.”
   (Publish-subscribe topic/criteria distribution).


Workflow & Activity Coordination: Three Work Units

1. Work Order: A unit of work where a human is doing something physical or operational
   (e.g., clean bed 4B, transfer patient to X-ray, draw blood sample).
2. To Do: A unit of work where a human is reviewing, updating, or deciding, including
   clinical approvals, sign-offs, and triage reviews.
3. Task: A unit of non-human executable work (internally a synthetic task) executed by plat-
   form automation, daemons, or services. Execution Semantics: Workflow Management pro-
   vides the coordination and state engine through which these three activity types progress.


Clinical Collaboration Context

Clinical Collaboration is Harmonia-Core because Harmonia provides Longitudinal Health
Record (LHR)-aware collaboration spaces. Clinicians can converse within secure multi-
disciplinary team rooms and query patient context directly (e.g., ”What were Fred’s last three
HbA1c results?”). Important Boundary: A clinical statement made within a collaboration chat
does not automatically become an authoritative clinical Observation or medical record entry.
It remains collaborative discourse unless formally authored into a clinical document.

Health Service Assurance: Approved Business Enabling Capabilities

REQ-FND-005 — Independent Assurance of Governed Activity motivates BC-18 — Health Ser-
vice Assurance. BC-18 requires the three Business Enabling Capabilities defined here. They
are collaboratively realised by the approved contributions of existing Enterprise Capabilities
and EC-14 — Service Guardian, as recorded in the contribution matrix.
These are Strategy capabilities and semantic boundaries. Their presentation does not create a
sixth contextual view, allocate them to an existing view, establish CT1 / CT2 / CT3 ancestry, or
derive Business Functions, Services, Processes, Features or assurance Information Concepts.


Assurance Design

• Definition: The capability to determine and define how satisfaction of a governed require-
  ment, constraint or expected behaviour will be assured, including its assurance disposition,
  applicable criteria, required evidence and evaluation expectations.
• Fundamental Question: How will satisfaction of this requirement, constraint or
  expected behaviour be assured?
• Boundary: Assurance Design is a peer concern to Behaviour Design and Failure/Recovery
  Design when implementing governed behaviour. This relationship establishes design con-
  cerns, not additional capability entries, application design or implementation specifications.


Assurance Criteria Management

• Definition: The capability to establish and manage reusable, governed and temporally iden-
  tifiable assurance criteria through which subjects may be evaluated.
• Scope: Criteria may express governance rule boundaries, quality constraints, performance
  expectations, compliance criteria, temporal criteria, evidence requirements or completeness
  expectations. These are examples, not an exhaustive taxonomy.




RAD-only baseline · 15 October 2026                                                         372
Harmonia EA Capability Map                                                       Version 0.1


• Boundary: Criteria management does not own or replace the authoritative governance
  requirement from which a criterion may derive. Not every assurance criterion is required to
  derive from formal Governance. Criteria may have their own lifecycle, version and temporal
  applicability.

    Assurance Criteria may operationalise a governing requirement for eval-
    uation, but SHALL NOT silently alter, weaken, strengthen or replace the
    authoritative requirement from which they derive.


Governed Assurance

• Definition: The capability to independently evaluate a governed subject against applicable
  assurance criteria through the assembly and evaluation of sufficient trustworthy evidence,
  establishing explicit findings, exceptions and assurance conclusions.
• Fundamental Question: What can we independently establish about this subject
  against these criteria from the available trustworthy evidence?
• Assurance Semantics: Establishing the subject/context of assurance, applicable assur-
  ance criteria, evidentiary association, assessment, adjudication, findings, exceptions and
  conclusions.
• Boundary: Governed Assurance does not manage, remediate, assign, delegate, escalate
  operationally or complete the subject activity. It may manage its own assurance activ-
  ity; findings may inform operational response without transferring responsibility for that
  response.


Assurance Disposition

Every implemented behaviour has an assurance aspect. Every governed obligation, functional
requirement, non-functional requirement or other defined implementation requirement SHALL
have an explicit assurance disposition identifying how its satisfaction is assured.
The approved disposition concepts are:

• Generic Assurance sufficient
• Existing Specific Assurance applies
• Existing Assurance must be extended
• New Specific Assurance required
• Not Assurable
• Not Worth Assuring

These are architectural semantics, not an information model or software enumeration. Not As-
surable does not mean the requirement is not required. Not Worth Assuring does not mean
the requirement is optional or unimportant. Both are explicit governed assurance decisions,
not absence of assurance configuration. An explicit disposition does not require specific as-
surance of every individual activity, information item or outcome; REQ-FND-005 applies where
assurance is required.


Generic Processing Assurance and System Operations

Harmonia-managed workflow behaviour SHALL be subject to applicable generic processing as-
surance. This concerns business-level processing behaviour above and beyond System Op-
erations. Potential concerns include progression, completion, timeliness, expected processing
pathway, failure behaviour, recovery behaviour, outcome, and aggregate or pattern behaviour.
This is not a final exhaustive criteria catalogue.
System Operations asks whether the technical machinery is operating. Generic processing
assurance asks whether governed business behaviour is operating within expected boundaries.
    Operational Health ≠ Processing Assurance.



RAD-only baseline · 15 October 2026                                                      373
Harmonia EA Capability Map                                                               Version 0.1


Failure and recovery are part of the expected behavioural space of the activity being executed.
The activity/Praxis remains responsible for handling its own expected failure and recovery be-
haviour. Assurance independently establishes whether normal, failure and recovery behaviour
remain within applicable expectations. This responsibility boundary does not allocate assur-
ance execution to Praxis or another solution construct.
EC-12 Operational Assurance retains its established resilience, concurrency, exception/
recovery and telemetry responsibilities and may contribute directly to generic operational/
processing assurance. EC-14 Service Guardian supplies the distinguishing assurance-specific
semantics; neither replaces System Operations or the other Enterprise Capability.


Assurance Evidence Assembly and Information Ownership

Assurance Evidence Assembly is the evidence-assembly concern within Governed Assurance;
this statement does not establish a fourth Business Enabling Capability or a downstream Func-
tion, Service or Information Concept.
Underlying information used as assurance evidence remains owned and managed by the ca-
pability responsible for that information. Assurance owns the contextual association that par-
ticular information constitutes evidence for a particular assurance purpose. Being evidence is
contextual, not an intrinsic universal property of source information.
Evidence may be associated through reference, linkage, aggregation, representation, mirroring
or derivation. These possibilities do not prescribe technical storage or replication. An associa-
tion may identify a particular version, state or temporal context of the underlying information.
     Evidence inclusion may be temporally and version-specific. Association of
     information as assurance evidence SHALL be capable of distinguishing the
     particular information state relevant to the assurance activity from the in-
     formation’s current state.


Temporally Appropriate Evidence and Criteria

Applicable assurance criteria may themselves be versioned and temporally applicable. A con-
clusion may depend both on the information state relevant to the evidence and on the criterion
state applicable to the subject at the relevant time. Assurance evaluates temporally appropri-
ate evidence against temporally appropriate criteria. No persistence, active-state, replication
or retention mechanism is derived here.


Assessment, Adjudication and Explicit Insufficiency

Concern                 Fundamental question              Semantic boundary
Assessment              What does this evidence           May supply quantitative, qualitative,
                        demonstrate with respect to the   compound, temporal or
                        applicable criterion?             confidence-bearing information.
Adjudication            What assurance finding or         Establishes the finding or conclusion from
                        conclusion follows from that      assessed detail; it is distinct from
                        assessment?                       assessment and operational response.


Assurance SHALL NOT be reduced universally to PASS / FAIL / UNKNOWN. Insufficient evidence is
not equivalent to either satisfaction or non-satisfaction. Under REQ-FND-005, where available
evidence cannot establish the required assurance conclusion with sufficient confidence, that
inability and evidence insufficiency SHALL remain explicit.
An assurance activity may execute correctly while lacking sufficient evidence to establish a
conclusion about its subject. This is distinct from an indeterminate execution outcome or exe-
cution failure. REQ-FND-004 and AX-15 continue to govern uncertainty about operational state,
effect or outcome, including the assurance activity’s own execution where applicable.




RAD-only baseline · 15 October 2026                                                              374
Harmonia EA Capability Map                                                           Version 0.1


Assurance Independence

Independent Assurance is performed through an independently governed activity whose pro-
gression and assurance conclusion are not controlled by the activity or mechanism responsible
for performing or managing the subject being assured.
Independence does not require a different organisation, person, application, Kubernetes clus-
ter or database, an external auditor, or physical separation. The subject activity may supply
evidence but SHALL NOT solely determine, suppress, manufacture or retrospectively alter its
own assurance conclusion.
     Evidence dependency does not compromise assurance independence; con-
     trol dependency does.
Assurance may manage its own assurance activity without assuming management of the sub-
ject activity. No technical or organisational separation is prescribed by this boundary.


Clinical Services Delivery Assurance Boundary

Health Service Assurance SHALL NOT be represented as Clinical Services Delivery Assurance.
Harmonia does not thereby assume responsibility for assuring clinical judgement, professional
practice, clinical adequacy of care, or delivery of clinical services by healthcare practitioners
or healthcare organisations.
Information concerning clinical service delivery MAY be the subject of governed assurance
where an explicit applicable requirement establishes that concern. This does not transfer re-
sponsibility for Clinical Services Delivery Assurance to Harmonia. Capability 06 — Clinical Qual-
ity, Safety & Improvement retains its established clinical quality/safety responsibilities.
     Harmonia may assure facts and behaviour concerning clinical activity where
     explicitly required; it does not thereby assure the clinical adequacy of care.


Strategy Derivation Boundary

The approved derivation view stops at collaborative Enterprise Capability realisation. No strate-
gic logical or application component is allocated these capabilities or EC-14. No Dokimasia,
Ponos, Praxis, Pragma, Digital Twin, Mneme, Mnemosyne, Calliope, Iris, Pylai or other implemen-
tation relationship is established. Business Architecture, Information Architecture and solution
derivation remain subsequent activities.


Downstream Progression

The Business Enabling Capability catalogue and its atomic Features establish what systems
must enable for the healthcare enterprise. These features serve as the empirical basis for
deriving the reusable, technology-neutral platform capabilities:

• Enterprise Capabilities (EC-01 .. EC-14): The established EC-01 through EC-13 and approved
  EC-14 Service Guardian; the Health Service Assurance contribution model is established
  without adding Feature or component allocations.
• Health Service Assurance Derivation: REQ-FND-005 → BC-18 → the three approved Business
  Enabling Capabilities → collaborative Enterprise Capability realisation.
• Capability Tier Progression Model: Detailed vertical derivation rules and representative com-
  position examples.
• ICT Foundation Lenses: Technical enablement considerations guiding technology realization.

Business Architecture Metamodel & Modelling Rules

1. Overview & Metamodel Hierarchy

The Harmonia Business Architecture metamodel defines the structural and behavioural rela-
tionships governing how healthcare capabilities are operationalised into functions, exposed
services, stateful processes, and information responsibilities.
RAD diagram: textual source notation.
graph TD
    subgraph OWNER["Owning Business / Business Enabling Capability or Feature responsibility context"]
         subgraph BC["Business Capability"]
             BC1["BC CT1"] -->|Decomposes| BC2["BC CT2"]
             BC2 -->|Decomposes| BC3["BC CT3"]
         end
         subgraph BEC["Business Enabling Capability"]
             CT1["BEC CT1"] -->|Capability decomposition| CT2["BEC CT2"]
             CT2 -->|Capability decomposition| CT3["BEC CT3"]
             CT3 -->|Frames every Harmonia Feature| FT["FT Feature<br/>(Capability Specialisation)"]
         end
         BC -.->|Enabled-by / supported-by where established| BEC
    end
    OWNER -->|Delivers| FUNC["Business Function(s)"]
    OWNER -->|Provides to clients| SERV["Business Service(s)"]
    SERV -->|May use directly| FUNC
    SERV -->|May use| PROC
    FUNC -->|May require| PROC
    PROC -->|Chains| FUNC
    OWNER -->|Encompasses where progression is material| PROC["Business Process(es)"]
    OWNER -->|Establishes| INFO["Business Information Responsibility"]

The diagram distinguishes two Capability hierarchies and preserves the permissible behavioural
responsibility contexts. Business Capabilities describe organisational abilities; Business En-
abling Capabilities describe reusable enabling abilities Harmonia provides or supports. Enable-
ment/support is not decomposition or implementation equivalence, and the aggregate diagram
establishes no individual BC↔BEC mapping. Business Capability decomposition does not termi-
nate in Harmonia Features. Every fully reconciled Harmonia Feature requires complete Busi-
ness Enabling CT1 → CT2 → CT3 ancestry. Functions, Services and Processes may still anchor
directly at their established owning Capability or Feature; they do not require an intervening
Feature. Service, Function and Process form a graph rather than a mandatory hierarchy. A
Function need not have either a Service or a Process.


1.1 Capability Decomposition and Terminology

The following terminology SHALL be used canonically:
 Term                                    Meaning
 Layer / Architectural Layer             Architectural layering within the TOGAF / ArchiMate architecture
                                         model.

Term                               Meaning
Capability Tier                    Hierarchical decomposition within a Capability Model.
Derivation / Derivation            Progression between different architectural constructs or models.
Progression                        A Derivation Stage is a stage in that progression.
CT1                                Capability Tier 1: establishes the broad Capability frame within
                                   Harmonia’s architectural scope.
CT2                                Capability Tier 2: decomposes the CT1 frame into constituent
                                   Capabilities.
CT3                                Capability Tier 3: establishes the finest Capability frame required
                                   by Harmonia. Within the Business Enabling hierarchy, CT3

FT                                 Feature: expresses required system-enabled behaviour within its
                                   owning Business Enabling CT3 Capability context.


Layer≠CapabilityTier≠DerivationStage. L1, L2 and L3 are deprecated as canonical capability
classifications.
Harmonia SHALL use the fixed three-tier Capability decomposition:
RAD source listing (presentation only; no inferred ancestry).
      Business Capability CT1 → CT2 → CT3
      enabled-by / supported-by
      Business Enabling Capability CT1 → CT2 → CT3 → FT Feature
Every Harmonia Feature SHALL be immediately framed by a Business Enabling CT3 Capa-
bility. Every established CT3 SHALL have a CT2 parent and every CT2 a CT1 parent within the
same Capability category. Capability tiers SHALL NOT be skipped. Complete Business Enabling
CT1 → CT2 → CT3 ancestry is required for a fully reconciled Feature; direct CT1 → FT and CT2
→ FT framing SHALL NOT be used. Business Capability CT3s do not require or own Harmonia
Features. An intentionally undecomposed BC branch does not indicate missing Feature framing.
      A Feature cannot compensate for incomplete Capability decomposition. If
      Harmonia requires a Feature, the CT3 Capability that frames that Feature
      must first be identified. Failure to identify a meaningful CT3 indicates in-
      complete upstream Capability modelling, not permission to skip the tier.
Complete decomposition is a modelling obligation, not authority to fabricate architectural el-
ements. CT3 Capabilities SHALL NOT be manufactured merely to satisfy structural symmetry.
Where an existing branch contains a Feature without an established CT3 frame or complete an-
cestry, the Feature, its established responsibility and local identifier SHALL be preserved, and
its Capability ancestry/decomposition SHALL be recorded as requiring reconciliation under AX-
17. It SHALL NOT be presented as fully reconciled or silently reattached to an invented owner.
Established partial relationships remain valid evidence until separately adjudicated.
A Feature remains a finer-grained Capability Specialisation within Business Enabling respon-
sibility and inherits Capability semantics. This retained classification does not make FT another
Capability Tier, a Business Capability child or an arbitrary-depth frame. CT1 → CT2 and CT2
→ CT3 denote same-category Capability decomposition; Business Enabling CT3 provides the
mandatory Feature frame. BC↔BEC support relationships do not supply missing ancestry in
either hierarchy.
CT3 is Harmonia’s intentional Capability decomposition boundary. Harmonia’s Capability Model
is bounded to the level required to derive and govern Harmonia; it does not attempt to model
the complete Enterprise Architecture of a hospital, health service provider, health department
or other healthcare enterprise. Harmonia SHALL NOT define CT4, CT5 or deeper Capability
tiers. Further detail is not authority to extend the Capability hierarchy.
Established higher-tier ancestry SHALL be represented in a lower-tier Capability’s Canonical ID.
Every Feature’s complete structural Canonical ID SHALL include its CT1, CT2 and CT3 ances-
try. An unidentified ancestor SHALL NOT permit omission of that tier; required but unresolved
ancestry SHALL leave the Canonical ID unresolved, as specified in §8.
